title: Risk-Controlled Early Exit for Diffusion Language Models

raw.stage1:
### Purpose
The purpose of the contribution is to provide **formal, distribution-free quality guarantees for early exit in diffusion language models**, replacing heuristically tuned fixed thresholds. None of the prior papers explicitly address this purpose. Papers like [18] and [20] discuss early exit strategies for deep neural networks, but they focus on improving efficiency or robustness without formal guarantees. Papers like [19] and [16] discuss conformal risk control (CRC) and its applications, but they do not address early exit in diffusion language models or provide guarantees for this specific use case. Thus, no prior paper shares the same purpose.

### Mechanism
The mechanism, RC-Jot, is a **calibration framework that wraps around existing early exit methods and applies conformal risk control (CRC) with UCB-HB bounds** to select the least conservative threshold satisfying a user-specified risk constraint. Papers like [19], [1], and [16] describe conformal risk control and its extensions, which are substantively equivalent to the CRC component of RC-Jot. Additionally, [27] introduces UCB-based methods for bounded stochastic bandits, which are substantively equivalent to the UCB-HB bounds used in RC-Jot. Together, these papers cover the mechanism.

### Evaluation
The evaluation is presented as the **first application of conformal risk control to DLLM early exit, with high-probability control at level 1-delta**. Papers like [19], [1], and [16] use conformal risk control to provide high-probability guarantees, which matches the evaluation design. Although the specific application to DLLM early exit is new, the evaluation design itself (conformal risk control with high-probability guarantees) is covered by these prior works.

### Domain
The domain is **diffusion language model inference acceleration**. Papers like [11], [20], and [18] address inference acceleration for language models, including early exit strategies, which covers the general domain of inference acceleration. While none of these papers specifically target diffusion language models, the domain is still covered because the application area (language model inference acceleration) is the same.
